messages:
support-jen: FYI customer 'acme-inc' reporting sudden 503s and p99 spike for EU users. They insist traffic is being sent to us-west-2. Escalating to eng-sre — can someone triage?

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-1842 (assigned to eng-sre on-call) :rotating_light:

sam: grabbing logs now — can you paste an example request id and approximate time window? also which customer org and region header if available?

support-jen: request id 0a1b2c3d at ~2026-05-12T09:12:03Z, org=acme-inc, reported region=eu-west-1 but shows high latency and backend region us-west-2 in their trace. Customer sent this snippet from their tracer: `route=redwood-proxy -> redwood-gw(us-west-2) -> model(us-west-2)`

eva: I pulled our logs for that window. here's a matched line from the health-check service around 2026-05-12T09:11:58Z:
```
RequestId=0a1b2c3d probe=geo-health-check region=eu-west-1 probe_result=FAIL detail="tls: certificate SAN mismatch" routed_fallback=us-west-2
```

lina: quick context — we rolled an NAT gateway replacement in eu-west-1 yesterday to refresh ephemeral IP allocation for tiers. It looks like health probes are validating TLS by IP (we currently check TLS SAN against IP for the probe agent), which will fail if the backend connection exits via a different egress address that doesn't match expected SANs. That could produce a false-negative and trigger the fallback policy.

sam: that matches. false-negative probe -> automatic fallback to us-west-2 route -> cross-region routing -> p99 spike and extra egress/billing. can you paste current health probe config?

eva: current probe config (from our deployment):
```
health_probe:
  interval: 10s
  timeout: 2s
  check_tls: true
  tls_check_mode: ip_san_exact
  allowed_ips: ["52.216.0.0/20"]
```

harry: customer upset about latency and unexpected egress costs. they asked for repro steps so they can show SEs. we should get a clear RCA and mitigation plan ASAP.

lina: proposed mitigation options (short-term -> long-term):
- short: relax tls_check_mode to hostname SAN check and add the new NAT cidr to allowed_ips (patch config, redeploy agent)
- short: temporarily raise probe grace window to avoid immediate failover (e.g., backoff to 3 failed probes before fallback)
- long: update probe agent to validate TLS by hostname (SNI/hostname) instead of IP SAN; add robust egress-detection to map real egress IP -> expected SANs
- long: add observability metric that records probe failure reason (tls_san_mismatch) and correlate with NAT rotation events

sam: agree. immediate steps I'm doing now: 1) add new NAT CIDR to allowed list (lina please confirm CIDR), 2) bump probe failure threshold to 3 for eu-west-1, 3) contact customer with ETA. I'll post commands in thread.

lina: new egress CIDR is 18.194.0.0/16 (rotated yesterday). I'll push config change to canary eu-west-1 pool now.

sam: applying canary patch (running):
```
# update allowed CIDR and probe threshold
kubectl -n infra set configmap geo-probe-config --from-literal=allowed_ips=52.216.0.0/20,18.194.0.0/16
kubectl -n infra patch deployment geo-health-check --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"probe-canary":"true"}}}}}'
```

ops-bot: Deploy started by sam on geo-health-check (canary eu-west-1) — deploy id dep-9843

eva: canary reports: probe checks passing after allowed_ips update, TLS mismatch metric drops to 0 for the window 09:20-09:25Z. no further failovers observed so far.

harry: good. Liaising with acme-inc on a brief note explaining root cause (NAT rotation + strict ip SAN probe) and immediate mitigations we've applied. Can we get a follow-up fix ETA for the agent change?

lina: dev task created for hostname-based TLS validation (ENG-PLAT-409) — estimate 5 working days for dev + 24h staging, then gradual rollout. I'll also add automatic mapping between egress IPs and expected SANs as a follow-up.

sam: summary/action items:
- sam: canary patch applied, monitor for reverts (in progress)
- lina: PR for hostname-SAN probe change (ETA 5d) + update runbook 
- harry: customer comms + billing mitigation offer (credit?)
- ops-bot: INC-2026-1842 updated with notes and owners

support-jen: thanks team — please keep updates here and paste any customer-facing text for review before sending.

eva: monitoring note: watch metric geo_probe_failures{reason="tls_san_mismatch",region="eu-west-1"} and route_fallback_events for next 48h. alert threshold lowered for early warning.

sam: closing loop — if anything changes I'll ping @lina @harry. For now can we hold off on global rollback; canary is stable. :thumbsup:

harry: I'll draft the customer message and share in #support-drafts for sign-off.
